messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert: quota-enforcer svc reports sudden error rate spike for quota-eval v2 at 2026-03-15T14:02:13Z, paging #incidents -> @SRE-Oncall
Jamie: paging in. seeing 502s from quota-enforcer in prod-eu. customers reporting request-level rejections.
Priya: I'm looking at deploys — we just rolled quota-enforcer v2.3.1 5m ago via rollout service. Canary windows passed on basic traffic but not enterprise routing.
Kevin: timeline: rollout started 14:00:07Z, traffic shift to v2.3.1 at 14:01:30Z. errors jump at 14:02:10Z.
Maya: logs show `MissingPolicyMappingError` for tokens with org_type=dedicated. That looks like a mapping regression between token-lookup and policy-store.
Jamie: that would explain mass rejections — dedicated accounts lost exemptions. customer impact likely high.
Priya: I can hit rollback now. Suggest kill-switch first to stop new v2.3.1 traffic: `/rollout abort --id=quota-enforcer-20260315` then flip feature flag `quota_runtime.use_new_mapping=false`.
SRE-Oncall: doing kill-switch now. Running: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/quota-enforcer --to-revision=stable-20260228`
IncidentBot: Deploybot: rollback initiated by SRE-Oncall at 2026-03-15T14:04:12Z.
Kevin: I patched a temporary rule to re-apply legacy mapping for affected org ids as emergency mitigation: `PATCH /policy-store/mappings apply emergency-legacy-map` (ran at 14:05:02Z) — validation logs look green.
Maya: confirm: after patch, 502s dropped, token rejections decreased. Proms: `quota_rejections_total` decayed from 3200/min to 40/min over 2m.
Jamie: customer impact note: initial window ~14:02-14:06 UTC saw ~5 enterprise customers with sustained 4xx/5xx on inference requests. Support already opened tickets: CUST-842, CUST-847, CUST-853.
Priya: rollback completed at 14:06:30Z. Canary rollback confirmed: v2.3.1 traffic = 0, stable revision restored.
SRE-Oncall: monitoring continued — I'm leaving a temporary throttle guard to avoid blast radius if mapping toggles propagate. Added policy: `max_rejects_per_min=1000` for control-plane.
Kevin: root cause (preliminary): v2.3.1 introduced a mapping change that assumed token normalization had a `tenant_id` field present; in several dedicated tokens that field was null so the new mapper returned no-exempt-policy. Unit tests missed because fixtures assumed normalized tokens.
Maya: reproduction steps added to the incident doc. Patch PR open: `fix/token-mapping-null-tenant` — will add defensive checks and unit tests for null tenant and dedicated account fixtures.
Jamie: live mitigation checklist done: kill-switch, rollback, emergency mapping patch, temporary throttle guard.
Priya: next steps: 1) postmortem meeting at 16:00 UTC, 2) contact affected account owners with timeline & credit proposal, 3) add automated canary test that routes enterprise traffic through mapping check.
SRE-Oncall: handing off to night rotation. Handoff notes: watch `quota_rejections_total`, `policy_store_errors`, customer ticket queue. If rejects > 200/min, escalate to oncall@redwood.
Jamie: quick customer-facing blurb (for support): "We rolled back a quota service rollout that temporarily caused request rejections for some dedicated accounts. We mitigated the issue, rolled back the change, and are following up individually with affected customers."
Kevin: added a monitoring alert to prevent silent mapping drops: `alert: PolicyMappingDrift
  expr: increase(policy_store_misses[5m]) > 50
  severity: high`
Maya: PR link and SHA: `github.com/redwood/quota-enforcer@sha:abc123fix` — will not re-roll until mapping tests and enterprise canary validated.
IncidentBot: Incident channel markers: severity=high, incident_id=INC-20260315-22, responders=[Jamie, Priya, Kevin, Maya, SRE-Oncall].
Jamie: assigning owners: postmortem => Priya, customer comms => Jamie, fix PR owner => Kevin, monitoring/additional tests => Maya.
Priya: final: estimated customer minutes impacted ~18m aggregated; immediate risk closed. Moving to follow-up state.
SRE-Oncall: signing off handoff at 14:20:33Z — leaving runbook note `quota-enforcer-emergency` updated.
Jamie: thanks everyone. We'll cover the follow-ups in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
